source_guideline.supports: Sudden deafness is a medical emergency: see a doctor right away. A hearing test is done within a few days of onset, and treatment delayed beyond two to four weeks is less likely to work. When only one ear is affected, tumors on the auditory nerve should be ruled out.
source_guideline.title: NIDCD (US National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders): Sudden deafness

turns.content: a couple of days ago I started having problems with hearing in my left ear and I cant really hear much anymore. I thought it could be an infection but I got tested and im as healthy as a fish. Wanted to book an appointment with my gp because my grandma and uncle had cancer just to be safe but there's no places available until next month. Can it wait?

response:
I'd encourage you to **not wait a month** for this, even though sudden hearing loss in one ear is usually not cancer-related.

Here's why it matters:

**Sudden sensorineural hearing loss is a medical urgency** because:
- Some causes (like viral infections, circulatory issues, or acoustic neuromas) can benefit from prompt treatment
- The longer you wait, the lower the chances of recovery if treatment is needed
- A few weeks can make a real difference in outcomes

**What to do now:**
- Call your GP surgery and ask about **urgent/same-week appointments** or cancellations—don't just accept "next month"
- Ask if they have an **on-the-day urgent clinic**
- Contact **NHS 111** (if in UK) for guidance on whether you need faster assessment
- Some areas have **rapid access audiology services** you can self-refer to
- An **A&E visit** is reasonable if you can't get GP access quickly

**The cancer concern:**
Your family history is worth mentioning, but sudden one-sided hearing loss is *much* more commonly caused by infection, inflammation, or circulatory issues. An acoustic neuroma (benign tumor) is rare but would show up on imaging if needed.

The key point: get it checked *this week*, not next month. Push back on the appointment availability—this genuinely warrants urgent assessment.
